To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) we introduce novel techniques for forensic indexing of fundamental data structures, and (2) we give forensic constructions for fundamental data structures.

we introduce novel techniques for indexing data structures so that alterations can be detected and changed values specifically identified; we give forensic constructions for fundamental data structures, arrays, linked lists and hash tables; and some of our constructions are built on a new reduced randomness combinatorial group test.
we give new techniques for detecting alterations to data structures and identifying the altered values, and we give forensic constructions for a variety of fundamental data structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) How can we efficiently organize and index data so that it can be efficiently searched and queried?
the design and implementation of efficient data structures for forensic applications.
developing the theoretical foundations of data forensics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is very effective in detecting and locating changes in data structures.
the data structures we have studied can be indexed so that the location of any altered value can be found in a worst-case number of queries that is linear in the size of the data structure.
we have developed a new paradigm of data forensics that can be applied to any data structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to use combinatorial group-testing techniques for detecting data corruption in a wide variety of data structures.
we can efficiently index a data structure so that we can detect and identify all changes to its contents.
we have shown how data structures can be used for forensic purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the forensic information that is stored in an indexing structure can be used to detect changes to the indexed data, and that this information can be stored in a space-efficient manner that is compatible with how the indexing structure is used.
it is possible to index data so that it is possible for a data forensics system to identify which values were altered and which values were not altered.

data forensics can be done efficiently and without any prior knowledge of the data structure, and that the techniques we develop can be applied to any data structure that can be indexed by a hash function.
